useCases.title: Agent Checkpoint: Verified Delegation for AI Agents
useCases.summary:
AI agents now act inside real people’s accounts: logging in, retrieving data, filling forms, transacting. Sites cannot tell a trusted agent from a malicious bot, so many block all automation and turn away legitimate customers. Agent traffic already runs 0.5% to 16% of customer traffic and grows monthly.

Vouched’s Agent Checkpoint ensures an agent only performs the actions its human authorized. Agent Checkpoint is built for agents: who is the human behind it, what did they permit, and an immutable audit trail proving what happened. Detect classifies agent traffic in real time. Enforce applies policy at the moment an agent acts: allow, step up authentication, or block. Govern records the delegation and consent chain.

It runs on KYA-OS, the open agent identity standard Vouched authored and donated to the Decentralized Identity Foundation with v1.0.0 in 2026.
useCases.userJourney:
A user asks an AI agent to pay an invoice. The agent calls the organisation's protected endpoint and is refused: needs_authorization, with a consent URL.

The human opens it and sees what's delegated: which agent (by DID), scope (payments.transfer), cap (10 CHEQ), 48h validity. On approval, the Responsible Party issues a W3C Verifiable Credential into the agent's wallet. The cap sits in the signed credential, not app code; a status-list entry is anchored on-chain.

The agent retries, its wallet signing a holder proof with the agent's did:key; the LLM holds no keys. The organisation verifies against the ledger: issuer DID document, status-list signature, purpose parity, expiry, holder binding, revocation bit, every call, ~0.8s. Payment executes from the organisation's own wallet, returning a detached-JWS receipt. Over-cap or stolen-credential attempts fail pre-handler.

To revoke, the human touches a FIDO2 key; the WebAuthn challenge is a hash of the revocation intent. An append-only status-list version publishes on-chain, so nobody can un-revoke quietly. Its next transfer is refused: CREDENTIAL_REVOKED.

Two wallets: the agent's credential wallet, the organisation's value wallet.
